beats.narration_en: Same emergency stop. Only one car can still steer.
Without ABS, slam the brakes and the wheels lock.
A sliding tire can't steer, so the car goes straight.
ABS watches how fast every wheel is turning.
The moment one starts to lock, it eases the brake, then squeezes again,
So the tires keep rolling, and they can still turn.
That buzz in the pedal? That's ABS working.
